==English==

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/məst/|/məs/|a=weak form}}
* {{IPA|en|/mʌst/|a=strong form}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-must.ogg|a=US}}
** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-must.wav|a=Southern England}}
* {{IPA|en|/mʊst/|a=Northern England,strong form}}
* {{homophones|en|mussed|musth}}
* {{rhymes|en|ʌst|s=1}}

===Etymology 1===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*med-}}{{etymid|en|hasto}}
From {{inh|en|enm|moste}} {{gloss|"must", literally, "had to", the past tense of {{der|en|enm|moten|t=to have to|id=to have to}}}}, from {{inh|en|ang|mōste||had to}}, 1st & 3rd person singular past tense of {{m|ang|mōtan||to be allowed, be able to, have the opportunity to, be compelled to, must, may}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*mōtaną}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|moest||had to}}, {{cog|de|musste||had to}}, {{cog|sv|måste||must, have to, be obliged to}}. More at ''[[mote#Etymology_2|mote]]''.

====Alternative forms====
* {{alt|en|mus'||dialectal}}

====Verb====
{{en-verb|~|-|~|-}} {{tlb|en|modal|_|auxiliary|defective}}

# {{senseid|en|modal auxiliary, for requirement, necessity, etc}} To do as a [[require]]ment; {{non-gloss|indicates that the sentence subject is [[required]] as an imperative or directive to execute the sentence [[predicate]], with failure to do so resulting in a failure or negative consequence}}.
#: {{ux|en|You '''must''' arrive in class on time.|q=the requirement is an imperative}}
#: {{ux|en|This door handle '''must''' be rotated fully.|q=the requirement is a directive, necessary to operate the handle.}}
#: {{ux|en|Everybody told me I '''must''' stop worrying, but I couldn't, because I knew that somehow there was still something wrong about the situation.}}
#: {{ux|en|You really '''must''' come and see us soon, pal. - We'll see: I can borrow my dad's car, but I '''must''' bring it back before midnight.}}
#: {{ux|en|The physician said that I '''must''' / had to / would [[have to]] stop smoking.}}
#* {{RQ:KJV|Acts|9|6|passage=Arise, and go into the city, and it shall be told thee what thou '''must''' do.}}
# {{senseid|en|modal auxiliary, for probability or certainty about past event}} To do with [[certainty]]; {{non-gloss|indicates that the speaker is [[certain]] that the subject will have executed the [[predicate]]}}.
#: {{ux|en|If it has rained all day, it '''must''' be very wet outside.}}
#: {{ux|en|Where would you have put the keyring? You couldn’t have lost it again! - I '''must''' have, because it's [[nowhere to be found]].}}
#: {{ux|en|I said it '''must''' be pretty late and I really must go.}}
#: {{ux|en|She's being taken to the [[police car]] now , so they '''must''' be [[going to]] arrest her.}}
# {{senseid|en|modal auxiliary, for probability or certainty about ongoing event}} {{n-g|Used to indicate that something is very likely, probable, or certain to be true.}}
#: {{ux|en|The children '''must''' be asleep by now.}}
#: {{ux|en|There's the doorbell. It '''must''' be Dad.}}

=====Usage notes=====
* {{sense|auxiliary|to do as a requirement}} Compare with weaker auxiliary verb {{m|en|should}}, indicating mere intent for the predicate’s execution; and stronger auxiliary verb {{m|en|will}}, indicating that the negative consequence will be unusually severe.
* {{sense|auxiliary|to do with certainty}} Compare with weaker auxiliary verb {{m|en|should}}, indicating a strong probability of the predicate’s execution.
* The past tense of “must” is also “must”. In main clauses, this use of the past tense is almost always literary (see King James Bible, Leiber, and Alcott quotations at [[Citations:must]]). In subordinate clauses, it is more common: ''I knew that he '''must''' come, but he never showed up.'' Otherwise, the past sense is usually conveyed by {{m|en|had to}}. It is possible to use ''was bound to'' for the past also. For this reason, {{m|en|have to}} and {{m|en|be bound to}} are also used as alternatives to {{m|en|must}} in the present and future.
* The principal verb, if easily supplied (especially ''go''), may be omitted. In modern usage this is mainly literary (see Housman and Tolkien quotations at [[Citations:must]]).
* {{m|en|must|Must}} is unusual in its negation: {{m|en|must not}} still expresses a definite certainty or requirement. {{m|en|need|Need}} and {{m|en|have to}}, on the other hand, are negated in the usual manner. Compare:
:: You '''must not''' read that book. (''It '''is''' necessary that you '''not''' read that book.'')
:: You '''need not/do not need to''' read that book. / You '''do not have to''' read that book. (''It '''is not''' necessary that you read that book.'').

===Etymology 2===
{{etymid|en|ferment}}
From {{inh|en|enm|must}}, from {{inh|en|ang|must}} and {{der|en|fro|must}}, {{m|fro|most}}, both from {{der|en|la|mustum}}.

====Noun====
{{en-noun|~}}

# The [[property]] of being [[stale]] or [[musty]].
# Something that [[exhibit]]s the property of being stale or musty.
# {{senseid|en|juice}} Fruit [[juice]] that will [[ferment]] or has fermented, usually from [[grape]]s (in [[winemaking]]) or [[apple]]s (in [[cidermaking]]).
#: {{ux|en|The guide then explained that the '''must''' drains from the [[cider press]] and runs into the vats where it will ferment.}}
